items.quote: said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse
items.contrast: Micah’s mother uttered the curse, while Micah took the silver and confessed the theft.
items.reason: Micah addresses his mother as “you” and says that he heard her utter the curse.

items.quote: took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the royal princes, who were about to be murdered. She put him and his nurse in a bedroom to hide him from Athaliah; so he was not killed. He remained hidden with his nurse at the temple of the Lord for six years
items.contrast: Joash remained with his nurse; Ahaziah was Joash’s deceased father, not the person in hiding.
items.reason: The repeated pronouns refer back to Joash son of Ahaziah, whom Jehosheba hid with his nurse.

items.quote: went to his mother’s brothers in Shechem and said to them and to all his mother’s clan, “Ask all the citizens of Shechem
items.contrast: His mother’s brothers and clan receive the instruction to pass on the message; the citizens of Shechem are its intended audience.
items.reason: The passage distinguishes the people Abimelek directly addresses from the citizens whom they are told to ask.

items.quote: was seeking a place of their own where they might settle, because they had not yet come into an inheritance among the tribes of Israel
items.contrast: Their lack of an inheritance is the stated cause; Israel’s lack of a king is only a surrounding circumstance.
items.reason: The causal word “because” directly links their search for land to their not yet having an inheritance.

items.quote: Let’s go at once and report this to the royal palace.
items.contrast: They plan to report the news to the palace, rather than continue their earlier taking and hiding of valuables.
items.reason: After recognizing that their conduct is wrong, the men explicitly propose going immediately to make a report.
